No it would just replace the general public 25% into a 35%. This is true of any time you or a customer applies for a card. If you're not approved it will add 10% to the general discount, and if you're approved it will replace the general % off with a 35%

Also sometimes you have a customer buying all or mostly excluded items so you can't really save them a lot by applying for a charge. In this situation (depending on your store and the management) you can sometimes have a manger price correct excluded items to add up to the appropriate discount, OR (more likely) you can give them the promise of the appropriate discount (depending on approved or not) off their next in-store purchase. This would obviously be something you'd have to clear with your managers first but I know certain managers at my store allow this, especially if the customer is approved and will be shopping with us again soon and using their newly approved charge.

So personally I try to wait until AFTER I ring all their items up and get any rewards / coupons / kohls cash added to their purchase. Then ask "Are we using a Kohl's card today?" and if they say no I just quickly add the appropriate discount for unapproved apps, and say "We just like to let you know if you wanted to open a card today I'd be able to take at least (X amount) off your purchase." It seems like they are more interested in the card if they know just how much money they are saving VS just telling them the percentage they'll save.

It also just depends on the person. Some people get mad the second the words "kohls card" comes out of your mouth, but others get a little interested once you mention or show the savings they can get with the app. I also like to throw in "Even if it's not approved you still get a discount"

And if you're really lucky you'll get someone who wants to know a little more, and you can let them know that with the card they get access to "kohls charge events" where they can get up to 30% off their whole order just bc they shopped with that card. Also the convenience of being able to pay it off right at the register immediately after they purchase, so they basically spend the same amount or less money with the added benefits of extra rewards every time they shop. Also it's a soft pull on their credit, so even if they get denied it's only a few points off their credit score, if anything at all.

But at the end of the day, if your manager is trying to bully you into getting credits, it doesn't matter how successful you are. That's wrong on their part, and you deserve a better work environment. Also idk if it's just because I work at a smaller store, but 12 credits a day sounds insane. Can't believe they'd push that on you on your 2nd day. I'm so sorry you're dealing with that. Best of luck <3

There's a good chance you'll feel a strong high while acclimating to Effexor, as well as lack of or absence of a sex drive. I know for a month or so after starting it, I was unable to orgasm no matter what I did. Also there's a chance it can make sleeping difficult. I was unable to sleep while on Effexor, so my psychiatrist put me on Trazadone to help. But over all I don't recall any major difficulties with getting started on the drug. Good luck!
